observations.note: 46 storeys + 3 bsmts. RC cols/beams, RC slabs, flat conc roof. internal walls masonry, core RC.
facade - unitised alu curtain wall, dbl glazed low-E / toughened. alu spandrels w 50mm rockwool. slab edge gap filled 135mm rockwool, 2hr. no combustible insulation on facade
office partitions drywall - gypsum, alu studs, rockwool infill
link to next bldg at B2 carpark, 2hr fire shutter. link not used, shutter perm shut

so the office floors are open plan, no separation within a floor except the utility rooms. elec rooms are 2 hour walls and floors with 2 hour doors, and every elec room we went into had the cable penetrations sealed
telecom risers triple vol, fire stopped every 3 flrs - the ones we saw ok. riser doors 1hr
internal stairs L27-29, L34-35, L40-41, L45-46. smoke det activated 2hr roller shutters round each stair
carpark all 3 bsmts, 351 lots + 6 accessible
tenant server room L5, approx 40 racks. UPS room next door, VRLA batteries. diesel genset at roof, 2 x 2000 kVA, day tank 1000 L, tested monthly on load per FM
3 x water cooled chillers B3, cooling towers on roof. 22 kV incomer from SP, 2 x transformers B1. no boilers. no hazardous storage apart from genset diesel
wet pipe sprinklers throughout incl car park, OH1 office / OH2 carpark. sprinkler tanks B3 2 x 300 m3. jockey + duty elec + standby diesel pump
few sprinkler heads recessed >50% into ceiling at B3 service corridor - obstructs spray pattern. FM said ceiling was lowered last yr
FM-200 in server room, last discharge/room integrity test 2023 - over due. no VESDA, only point smoke detectors
addressable fire alarm, monitored 24/7 by FCC on L1, direct link to SCDF. hose reels + extinguishers every floor, wet riser
weekly pump churn test logs ok but last annual flow test record not available. diesel pump fuel tank 3/4 full
bounded by public roads N and E, MRT station S (underground link closed off), 30 storey office W approx 25 m away
low lying area, PUB flood map - in flood prone zone. flood barriers at carpark ramp, manual, deployed by security on heavy rain warning. no flood since 2010 per FM
security 24/7, 6 guards per shift. CCTV ~300 cams recorded 30 days, monitored at FCC. card access turnstiles at lobby, lift destination control
loading bay manned 7am-10pm, after hours shutter locked + intruder alarm. carpark barrier + LPR
multi-tenant office, ~4000 occupants. building ERP exists, reviewed 2025, fire drill twice a yr. no BCP for the building itself - left to tenants. server room tenant has own DR site
CBD location, flat site approx 8,000 m2. SCDF fire stn ~2 km, response under 10 min per FM. hydrants on Rd N and E
construction site to the S across the road - 2 tower cranes, hot works on going. approx 40 m from our facade
lightning protection on roof, last tested 2025. windstorm - SG no typhoons, but sumatra squalls; roof plant tied down, curtain wall designed for wind load per FM
earthquake - SG low seismic zone, only tremors felt from sumatra quakes. no damage history. no seismic bracing on sprinkler pipes
B3 plant room + transformers in B1 below flood level. sump pumps x2 in B3, on genset supply, but no high water alarm to FCC

statements.text: Construction is rated Good: the building is of fire-resistive reinforced concrete construction with no combustible insulation on the facade.

Fire protection is rated Above Average: the building is fully sprinklered with an automatic fire alarm monitored around the clock, although some sprinkler heads in the B3 service corridor are recessed into the ceiling.
Management programs are rated Average: the server room's gaseous system is overdue for its room integrity test, and no annual pump flow test record was available.
External exposure is rated Average: the basements lie in a flood-prone zone protected only by manually deployed barriers, and an active construction site with hot work lies about 40 m to the south.
The main loss scenario considered is a fire in the Level 5 server room spreading to the adjoining UPS room, given the room's overdue gaseous system test and point-type smoke detection only.
A second scenario is flooding of the three basement levels, which hold the car park, chillers and transformers.
Loss figures are to be completed by the engineer from the site values.
Building Maintenance: Established. Building systems are maintained under the facility management contract, with no structural issues noted.
Electrical Maintenance: Embedded. Two 2,000 kVA generators are tested monthly on load, and electrical rooms were found sealed and in order.
Equipment Maintenance: Established. Chillers and cooling towers are maintained in the Basement 3 plant room.
Fire Protection Impairment Management: Formalized. Sprinkler heads in the B3 service corridor were left recessed after the ceiling was lowered, with no impairment record noted.
Fire Protection System Maintenance & Testing: Formalized. Weekly pump churn tests are logged, but no annual flow test record was available, and the server room's gaseous system test is overdue.
Emergency Response Planning: Embedded. The building's emergency response plan was reviewed in 2025, and fire drills are held twice a year.
Business Continuity Planning: Undeveloped. There is no business continuity plan for the building; continuity is left to the tenants.
Maintenance of building services is generally well established, but fire protection testing records and impairment controls need formalising, and the building has no continuity plan of its own.
The building comprises 46 storeys above ground and 3 basement levels, of reinforced concrete columns, beams and slabs with a flat concrete roof, and is of non-combustible construction.
The facade is a unitised aluminium curtain wall with double-glazed glass; the slab edge gaps are filled with 135 mm rockwool to a 2-hour fire rating, and no combustible insulation was noted.
Office partitions are of drywall with gypsum board on aluminium studs and rockwool infill.
Electrical rooms are enclosed by 2-hour fire-rated walls, floors and doors, and cable penetrations were sealed in every room entered.
Telecom risers are fire-stopped every three floors, and smoke-detector-activated 2-hour roller shutters enclose the internal stairs between tenant floors.
The Basement 2 link to the neighbouring building is closed off by a permanently shut 2-hour fire shutter.
No combustible construction materials were noted.
Occupancy: Multi-tenant office building with about 4,000 occupants and a three-level basement car park.
Server rooms: A tenant server room on Level 5 of about 40 racks, beside a UPS room with VRLA batteries.
Two 2,000 kVA diesel generators on the roof, with a 1,000 L day tank, provide back-up power.
Three water-cooled chillers in the Basement 3 plant room serve cooling towers on the roof.
Wet pipe sprinklers protect the whole building, including the car park.
Several sprinkler heads in the B3 service corridor are recessed more than 50% into a ceiling lowered last year, which obstructs their spray pattern.
The Level 5 server room is protected by an FM-200 system whose last room integrity test was in 2023 and is overdue.
A jockey pump, a duty electric pump and a standby diesel pump draw from two 300 m3 tanks in Basement 3; no annual flow test record was available.
An addressable fire alarm is monitored around the clock from the fire command centre on Level 1, with a direct link to the fire service.
North and East: Public roads, with public hydrants along both.
South: An active construction site about 40 m away across the road, with two tower cranes and ongoing hot work.
West: A 30-storey office building about 25 m away.
Public fire service: The nearest fire station is about 2 km away, with a response time under 10 minutes.
Flood: The site lies in a flood-prone zone; manual flood barriers at the car park ramp are deployed by security on heavy rain warnings.
Flood: The Basement 3 plant room and Basement 1 transformers sit below flood level; two sump pumps run on generator power, but there is no high water alarm to the fire command centre.
Windstorm: No typhoon exposure; roof plant is tied down against squalls and the curtain wall is designed for wind load.
Lightning: Lightning protection is installed on the roof and was last tested in 2025.
Earthquake: Low seismic zone with no damage history; sprinkler pipework has no seismic bracing.
Guards: Six guards per shift, around the clock.
About 300 CCTV cameras are recorded for 30 days and monitored from the fire command centre.
Access: Card-access turnstiles in the lobby, and a car park barrier with licence plate recognition.
Power: A 22 kV incomer feeds two transformers in Basement 1, with roof-top diesel generators as back-up.
Business Continuity Plans available?: No building-level plan; continuity is left to the tenants, and the server room tenant has its own disaster recovery site.
